definition: A training approach where the model itself selects which data points would be most informative to have labeled next, to minimize labeling cost while maximizing learning efficiency.
details: Active learning is especially valuable when labeling data is expensive or time-consuming, since it focuses human annotation effort on the examples the model finds most uncertain or informative.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Active Learning.
